Please explain the following content clearly and concisely:

**Backshift** (when the reporting verb is in the past):

|Direct|Reported|
|---|---|
|"I work here."|She said (that) she worked there.|
|"I am working."|She said she was working.|
|"I have finished."|She said she had finished.|
|"I will help."|She said she would help.|
|"I can swim."|She said she could swim.|

**No backshift needed** when the statement is still true / a general fact, or when the reporting verb is present.

## 3. Double comparatives

- "more simpler" → simpler
- "more easier" → easier

**Rule**: comparative adjectives take either "-er" OR "more," never both. This appeared twice in one essay — likely an interference pattern (possibly from a language where doubling intensifies, like Portuguese "mais fácil").
